ety.text: From French pyramide, from Old French piramide, from Latin pȳramis, pȳramidis, from Ancient Greek πῡραμίς (pūramís), possibly from πῡρός (pūrós, “wheat”) + ἀμάω (amáō, “reap”) or from Egyptian pr-m-ws (“height of a pyramid”), from pr (“(one that) comes forth”) + m (“from”) + ws (“height”). Schenkel and K. Lang proposed hypothetical Coptic *ⲡⲓⲣⲁⲙ (*piram) or *ⲫⲣⲁⲙ (*phram) derived from Egyptian mr via metathesis as a source of πῡραμίς (pūramís) while Schenkel also suggested it being the source of Arabic هَرَم (haram) although the latter is considered far-fetched by Takacs.

senses.d: An ancient massive construction with a square or rectangular base and four triangular sides meeting in an apex, such as those built as tombs in Egypt or as bases for temples in Mesoamerica.
A construction in the shape of a pyramid, usually with a square or rectangular base.
A solid with triangular lateral faces and a polygonal (often square or rectangular) base.
Any structure or diagram with many members at the bottom and progressively fewer towards the top.
ex: The company was organized as a pyramid, with a CEO in charge of four directors, each heading up a department.
They sit looking at the empty plate that had held a pyramid of sesame cakes. They have eaten them all.

senses.d: A medullary pyramid, the medial-most bumps on the ventral side of the medulla oblongata
The game of pool in which the balls are placed in the form of a triangle at spot.
The triangular layout of cards in the game of Pyramid.
ex: Build your pyramid with all cards face down, except the cards in the bottom row.

senses.d: An approximately triangular headline consisting of several centered lines of text of increasing length.
To build up or be arranged in the form of a pyramid.
ex: The paint was stacked in neatly pyramided lots along the concrete floor.

senses.d: To combine (a series of genes) into a single genotype.
To employ, or take part in, a pyramid scheme.

ex: Multiply this by the number of shares you traded, and add other positions if you pyramided.

senses.d: To increase to or towards a peak.

grp.label: in geometry, a solid with triangular lateral faces and a polygonal base
